chapter: Trummy Young's band, 52nd Street and the Navy
title: Opening on 52nd Street at the Yacht Club opposite Dizzy Gillespie and Coleman Hawkins
summary: The band plays the Yacht Club while Hawkins, Gillespie, Billie Holiday, Tatum and Red Allen work neighboring clubs.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: We went into the Capital Lounge in December, and we stayed there up through about March, I believe. And we left there and went to New York, 52nd Street, and opened up in another...if not more so. Because 52nd Street... The block we were working on, there were at least seven or eight clubs right on that block, and they were all right next door to each other. And each club had at least two or three bands working there.

On 52nd Street, we opened at a place called the Yacht Club. In the Yacht Club, our band worked opposite Dizzy Gillespie. Dizzy Gillespie and Coleman Hawkins had a band, and Jackie Miles playing drums, Oscar Pettiford on bass, and Clyde Hart on piano. There was a woman, Una Mae Carlisle, who sang in there. They had three attractions.

Across the street was Billie Holiday. I think Max Roach had a group over there, or Max Roach was playing with somebody over there or something. I don't remember who the other group was. But next door was Art Tatum, Red Allen, somebody else... These groups changed around quite a lot. A lot of times I'm thinking... I remember working in the club... Later on, after Roy came back from Chicago, he worked there, and Red Allen went across the street. It was one of those kind of things, you know. It was three groups in the Three Deuces.
After Dizzy and Coleman Hawkins left the Yacht Club, I
think Coleman Hawkins went into the Three Deuces, and Hot Lips Page came into the Yacht Club. The bands were always switching around like that.
